installation.note: head is a built-in command available on all Linux systems by default

overview.summary: head displays the first lines of files. It's the opposite of tail - while tail shows the end, head shows the beginning. Useful for checking file headers, seeing file structure, or previewing file contents.

syntax.description: Display first lines of FILE(s). Default shows first 10 lines. Multiple files can be specified.

options.use_case: Show first 50 lines instead of default 10

options.description: Display first N bytes instead of lines

misconceptions.title: head shows end of file
misconceptions.misconception: head displays the end of files
misconceptions.reality: head shows the BEGINNING of files. Use tail to see the end. head is perfect for checking file headers and structure.
misconceptions.tip: head = beginning of file, tail = end of file. head is most useful for file headers.

common_pitfalls.description: head on binary files shows garbled output
common_pitfalls.solution: head works best on text files. For binary files, use appropriate tools or hexdump.

related_commands.relationship: View end; head shows beginning, tail shows end
related_commands.description: Display last lines of files (opposite of head)

related_commands.relationship: View files; head for beginning, less for full file
related_commands.description: View entire files with scrolling (more powerful than head)

related_commands.relationship: View files; head for beginning, cat for all
related_commands.description: Display entire file contents (use head for large files)

best_practices: Use head to preview file structure and headers
Use -n to specify number of lines (default is 10)
Use head for CSV/data files to see column headers
Use head for config files to see structure
Combine with tail: head -n 1 file.txt (first line only)
Use head instead of cat for large files when you only need beginning
performance_tips: head is very fast - only reads beginning of file
Much faster than cat for large files (only reads first N lines)
Use head instead of cat when you only need file beginning

additional_notes.default_lines: Default shows first 10 lines. Use -n to change.
additional_notes.vs_tail: head shows beginning, tail shows end. Both are fast alternatives to cat for large files.
additional_notes.file_headers: Perfect for viewing file headers, CSV column names, config file structure
additional_notes.multiple_files: Can specify multiple files - each shown with header
additional_notes.common_pattern: Common pattern: head -n 1 file.csv (see header), head config.conf (see config structure)
